He who destroys the life of another human being, except in necessary self-defence, is judged condemned by the laws of God and man to be guilty of MURDER, and is punished accordingly. In what estimation ought we to hold that man, or that party, who wantonly plunges a nation into war and thereby occasions the destruction of hundreds and thousands of human lives in the forum of conscience, an attempt to murder either individually or nationally, equally criminal as the actual perpetration at the deed. This view of the subject naturally leads the mind to serious reflections upon the murderous policy promoted by Ross, Morris, &c. in Congress, to ruin us into an unjust and unjustifiable war with France and Spain by forcing her coasts, with an armed force, by way of reprisals for unauthorized inroads made upon the territory of that port. How can conscientious men any longer support that party in such a weak and wicked system of expense and bloodshed? It has now become a serious question of morality and confidence, as well as of policy, and as such it is recommended to the judicious consideration of every reader, especially those who have heretofore been blinded by the fair promises and pretensions of Federalists. The proposed seizure of New-Orleans would have been an act of hostilities against Spain, who was then in possession of the place, and also against France, to whom the right of property belonged; and the war, thus introduced, without a previous demand of reparation, or even would, according to the laws of nations, have been on our part unjustifiable, and the sacrifice of hundreds of thousands of lives, a bundle of millions of dollars, and ten times as much value in shipping and cargoes and interests and commerce, would not, according to the common course of human events, have afforded such bold indignation, as reasonably to be expected from pacific governments, to the existing state of Europe and this country. But the chance was, said I, as the desperate only chance of the Federalist party, that war might occasion such revenues, and interests, as to finance the Treasury, from ECONOMY, and aided by the desperate acts of aggression, eventually bring the administration into popular favor, and thereby lay a foundation for the Federalists to exist in power. Every pirate ought to repent; every Christian ought to return thanks to Almighty God, that Federalists have been once more defeated, and was avoided. Peace, justice, and liberties, provided by the people, stops a just cause.

Amen. [PROB. 1803.]
